answer: Sybil resistance runs on a bonded attestation thread. A key needs three unrelated operators to vouch before earning; each vouch locks stake slashed on proven forgery. A fake costs three bonds plus three independent operator ties, so a thousand fakes need three thousand bonds, draining when one link fails. The record is public: a duplicate collapses into the node it copies, so one vault address cannot repeat in the thread. Vouching for a bad key forfeits that stake and bars re-vouching. One detection ripples outward, seizing dependent bonds at once, so a fake's cost exceeds its yield.
